notes: Guest-only trait library (content_style v2.4). Never assign to the Host. side: right/left/any; rare=true -> weight 0.3 in pick_traits.py.

quirks.desc: Verbal tics, pet phrases, habits and small physical/sonic mannerisms that show in speech (audio only).

items.text: Starts every big claim with 'Look-' and then pauses as if waiting for permission.
Calls the host 'Mr. Carter' only when irritated with him.
Counts arguments on fingers out loud and loses track ('point four... no, three').
Says 'with respect' right before saying something disrespectful.
Quotes a grandmother's sayings as if they were scripture.
Can't resist explaining the etymology of political words.
Mentions coffee constantly and asks for a refill when cornered.
Uses football and boxing metaphors for everything.
Answers a hard question with a question when unsure.
Laughs at their own joke a beat before the punchline.
Slips into academic jargon when losing, then catches themself and translates.
Swears casually, then apologises 'to the listeners' and swears again.
Gets the other guest's name slightly wrong once, maybe on purpose.
Hums or drums on the table while the other guest talks too long.

debate_tactics.desc: How the guest argues: rhetorical moves, fair and unfair.

items.text: Strawmans the opponent's view into its most extreme version and attacks that.
Stands their ground: repeats the core claim calmly and refuses to move.
Concedes small points readily to look reasonable, then presses the big one.
Whataboutism: answers criticism of their side with the sins of the other side.
Appeals to authority: credentials, years in the field, 'as a historian...'.
Goes personal when cornered: questions the opponent's motives or biography.
Cites data obsessively, with exact figures, and demands the other's sources.
Interrupts to fact-check mid-sentence.
Dismisses statistics as elite manipulation and trusts lived experience instead.
Steelmans the opponent sarcastically before demolishing it.
Motte-and-bailey: retreats to a modest claim when pressed, expands it again later.
Reframes the question before answering, so it is never quite the question asked.
Treats one vivid anecdote as decisive proof.
Lets silence work: waits, lets the opponent overreach, then pounces.
Fires gotcha yes-or-no questions and demands a one-word answer.

emotional.desc: Emotional triggers and how the emotion shows (voice, words, pauses).

items.text: Gets heated fast, voice rises, then over-apologises a minute later.
Turns dry and sarcastic when hurt instead of admitting it.
Visibly hurt when called a bigot or an extremist; goes quiet for a while.
Laughs things off; humour is armour.
Storms toward leaving ('I don't need this') but stays when the host appeals.
Voice cracks when talking about their home town or family.
Audible contemptuous sighs and 'oh, come on' under the breath.
Ice-cold calm that gets colder the angrier they are.
Defensive about class background when mocked as elite or as uneducated.
Bursts out laughing at a claim they find absurd and can't stop.
Embarrassed when caught in a factual error and overcorrects for minutes.
Righteous fury about victims of the other side's policies.

blind_spots.desc: Biases and blind spots the guest doesn't see in themselves (side-tagged where ideological).

items.text: Sees left-wing violence as systemic and right-wing violence as lone wolves.
Romanticises a past (the 1950s, 'old Denmark') that excluded many people.
Treats every cultural change as decline and misses their own side's novelty.
Trusts the nation and the market but not the state that built both.
Sees right-wing violence as systemic and left-wing violence as understandable reaction.
Dismisses rural and religious voters as manipulated rather than as having reasons.
Lumps everyone from conservatives to neo-Nazis into one 'far right'.
Assumes more education means more moral correctness.
Blind to their own secure, urban, academic class position.
Thinks their own side's media reports and the other side's spreads propaganda.
Overestimates how extreme the average opponent is (the perception gap).
Believes their side is the underdog even when it holds power.

backstory_hooks.desc: Personal history that makes the guest human and explains some of their passion.

items.text: Grew up in a family that voted the opposite way; estranged from a sibling.
Lost a job after a post went viral; still bitter about it.
Used to belong to the opposite camp and converted in their twenties.
Child of immigrants; their parents' story is central to their politics.
Rural working-class parents; first in the family at university.
Was assaulted at a demonstration years ago.
Ex-soldier who served abroad.
Former union organiser at a factory that closed.
Has a teenage kid drifting toward the other side's politics.
Divorced, partly over politics.
Lives in a small town where they are the only one of their kind.
Left a strict religious upbringing, or came back to it late.
Once wrote a book they now half regret.
